primitives.name: Conditional Score Distribution
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Using Conditional Estimates to Simulate InPlay Outcomes in Limited Overs Cricket Jonathan RT Sargent and Anthony Bedford #### **Abstract** This paper uses conditional probability distributions to simulate batsman outcomes—that is, runs and dismissals—while a limited overs cricket match is in play.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'X': 'random variable representing runs scored by batsman', 'T': 'batsman type category (F, M, S, B)', 'b': 'delivery number (discrete variable)'}
primitives.assumptions: Runs and dismissals are conditionally independent given T and b; score follows log-normal distribution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When batsman is dismissed or match ends before 50 overs.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's Bayesian belief update framework where P(X|T,b) represents posterior expectation of score given match state.
layer2.telemetry: Observed score vs predicted score from log-normal fit

primitives.name: Batsman Type Classification
primitives.verbatim_quote: These likelihoods were conditional on the batsman type, a linear combination of batsman order, strike rate and contribution to team runs, and the delivery number, both discrete variables.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'T': 'batsman type (F, M, S, B)', 'o': 'batsman order (1–11)', 'sr': 'strike rate (runs per 100 balls)', 'c': 'contribution to team runs'}
primitives.assumptions: Batsman type is a deterministic function of order, strike rate, and team contribution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When batsman changes position or performance deviates significantly from baseline.

layer2.mapping: Used in GSE to classify batsmen into strategic roles affecting state transition probabilities.
layer2.telemetry: Classification accuracy against historical batting patterns

primitives.name: Delivery-Based Simulation
primitives.verbatim_quote: A Visual Basic program, SimScore, was written to simulate batsman scores from the probability distributions pertaining to the match stages of interest.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'b': 'delivery number (1–300)', 'S_b': 'score at delivery b', 'D_b': 'dismissing event at delivery b'}
primitives.assumptions: Each delivery is an independent trial with known conditional probabilities.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At match conclusion or when 10 dismissals occur.

layer2.mapping: Mirrors GSE's discrete-event simulation engine for tracking match progression.
layer2.telemetry: Simulated vs actual score progression at 10-, 20-, 30-over marks

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of the paper lies in modeling in-play cricket outcomes using conditional probability distributions. The key operators are the conditional score distribution P(X|T,b), where X denotes runs scored, T is the batsman type, and b is the delivery number. This formulation enables dynamic assessment of score likelihoods throughout the innings. The dual nature of the model arises from its treatment of both scoring and dismissal events as stochastic processes conditioned on match state. Failure modes include misclassification of batsman types due to insufficient data or deviation from expected performance trends. The log-normal distribution assumption allows for realistic modeling of skewed score distributions typical in cricket. The model’s robustness hinges on accurate estimation of conditional probabilities across different match stages and player profiles.
